title: Dragons, Castles, and an Irresistible Princess Bent on Revenge with Katherine Rundell
description:
Katherine Rundell’s award-winning Impossible Creatures soared to instant stardom, quickly earning the spot as one of the most popular children’s fantasy books in the 2020s. Now you can tune-in online to hear directly from the author (and ask your own questions about Christopher and Anya’s adventures) as we dive into the sequel, The Poisoned King!

Christopher Forrester woke to find a dragon chewing on his face—and his heart leapt for joy! He’d been dreaming of going back to the Archipelago, the secret cluster of islands where all the creatures of myth still live, and here was his summons.

But there is a poison spreading in the Archipelago. Rooting it out will involve a daring rescue mission on the back of a sphinx, a stealthy entrance to a dragon’s lair, and a death-defying plan to save a prisoner held in the heart of a castle. At the center of this storm is Anya: a small girl with a flock of birds at her side, a new-hatched chick in her pocket, and a ravenous hunger for justice.

Katherine Rundell’s second thrilling installment in the Impossible Creatures series involves castles, dragons, and revenge—the things of which great stories are made. The splendors within are brought to life with fifty illustrations, including a map and a bestiary of magical creatures.

Register now to go behind-the-scenes of the making of the Impossible Creatures books–just in time for The Neverfear’s (Book #3)’s release on September 1, 2026!

About the Author:

Katherine Rundell is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of Impossible Creatures and The Poisoned King. Her other books for children include Rooftoppers, Cartwheeling in Thunderstorms, The Wolf Wilder, The Explorer, and The Good Thieves. For adult readers, Rundell has written Vanishing Treasures: A Bestiary of Extraordinary Endangered Creatures and Super-Infinite: The Transformations of John Donne, which won the Baillie Gifford Prize for Non-Fiction. She has received the British Book Award for Book of the Year and Author of the Year. She grew up in Zimbabwe, Brussels, and London, and is currently a Fellow of St. Catherine’s College, Oxford.

title: Queer Lit Club
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This month we will be reading "We Burned So Bright" by TJ Klune. 

"Husbands Don and Rodney have lived a good long life. Together they've experienced the highest highs of love and family, and lows so low that they felt like the end of the world. Now, the world is ending for real. A rogue black hole is coming for Earth and in a month everything and everyone they've ever known will be gone. Suddenly, after 40 years together, Don and Rodney are out of time. They're in a race against the clock to make it from Maine to Washington State to take care of some unfinished business before it's all over. On the road they meet those who refuse to believe death is coming and those who rush to meet it. But there are also people living their final days as best they know how--impromptu weddings, bright burning bonfires, shared meals, and new friends. And as the black hole draws near, among ball lightning and under a cracked moon in a kaleidoscope sky, Don and Rodney will look back on their lives and ask if their best was good enough. Is it enough to burn bright if nothing comes from the ashes?"

title: History of the White House, America's Executive Mansion
description:
With Patricia Wells

Construction took eight years; a fire nearly destroyed it, it came dangerously close to collapsing, and someone almost painted it black. Although President Washington chose the design, he never really lived there. However, although Jefferson, Taft, and the Roosevelts made exceptional modifications, one of their genius architects came dangerously close to destroying the structure. It is the edifice that has been the most easily recognizable across the country for the past 225 years.

About the presenter

Patricia Wells, a historian and storyteller, regularly presents all around the state of New Jersey as part of her program called History Is Speaking. These lectures cover various local history topics, including the American Revolution, the Great Swamp, and courageous historical women. The public libraries and historical societies that host her presentations, both in person and virtually, are frequent hosts of her events.

This event will be held in the Community Room 1

title: Let's Walk!! the Pompton Valley Rail Trail
description:
Let's Walk!!
There's a new multi-use paved path in Pequannock, so let's check it out. Opened in 2025, it's one of Morris County Parks newest and largest trail initiatives.

We'll meet at 9:30 to walk to the northern terminus and back. It's about 3 miles and we'll finish in about 75 minutes.

Feeling strong and adventurous? Come at 7:00 and we'll walk to the southern end and back before the others join us. This section is an additional 7 miles to go out and back.

Bring water. Wear good shoes and a hat (some sections are quite exposed). There are several street crossings.

[Want more info? Click HERE](https://www.morrisparks.net/parks_trails/pompton-valley-rail-trail/)

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**
**We start promptly at the time posted.**

**Timeline:**
7:00 AM - walk begins southbound from Pequannock Valley Park
8:15 AM - return to start
**9:30 AM - regular Meetup event begins** \- walking northbound
10:30-11:00 AM - finish (depending on pace)

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: The Space for Words - Open Mic Night for Writers
description:
The Space for Words – literary open-mic night hosted by the NJ Poetry Circle
July 31  |  Doors open at 7:30, start time 8 pm  |  $10 for everyone 
This is a monthly event on the last Friday of every month, holidays permitting. 
Hey writers, poets, and storytellers!  Come share your art with us at The Space for Words Open Mic Night. Whether you’re a seasoned author or just getting started, this is your chance to share your work in front of a supportive and inspiring audience. 
Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work — the stage is yours! The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Each performer will have a few minutes to showcase their writing, followed by an opportunity to connect with fellow creatives. 
Come for the words, stay for the community. The Space for Words has grown into an amazing community of writers supporting one another. This event is open to all levels and all genres, so whether you write fiction, non-fiction, memoir, or poetry, we want to hear from you. It’s all about celebrating the power of storytelling in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. All of our open mic nights are always inclusive. 
Anyone who puts their name in the bucket upon entry gets a shot at the mic. You may be limited to about 10 minutes, depending on how many people sign up. Audience members are, as always, a welcome and vital part of the performances. 
If you have published books that you would like to sell, bring some copies and be prepared to accept payment. 
General guidelines: 

Hate speech of any kind is never allowed and will be shut down.
Violence or references to physical harm to others will be shut down.

BYOB is welcome, and some light snacks and drinks are served. 
Accessibility: The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building, accessible via a flight of stairs. Unfortunately, there is no elevator access at this time. This means we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs or guests with significant mobility challenges. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We meet at 9AM unless one or more people comment wanting to meet at 8AM which is my preferred time. You’re welcome to show up any time but are encouraged to post it so we have a better idea of what to expect for that day. (Those who share the same comment for start time can simply like that comment so we see how many show up for that time without potentially cluttering the comments.)

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll follow my Florida instructor’s method for balanced clinic matches\. This will typically include quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages team clotting\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

location: RecRoom, 1 Lackawanna Plaza, Ste. 6, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) 
LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. 
In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. 
Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. 
Kids will explore:
• Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components
• Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect)
• Testing, debugging, and iterating designs
• Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas 
Details:
• 60-minute session
• Small-group format
• No prior experience required 
Community Sponsorship:
20% of seats are reserved for community sponsorship. Families interested in sponsored spots can email info@kineticmindscreative.com
for details.

title: RUST - Film Screening and Discussion with Marylou & Jerome Bongiorno
location: Nutley - Children's Room, Nutley Free Public Library
description:
RUST:  Film Screening and Discussion
Saturday, August 1, at 2:00 p.m.

Discussion will follow the film screening with award-winning filmmakers Marylou & Jerome Bongiorno and Special Guest, Edwin Ortiz

RUST (Documentary, 2021, 86 min.) RUST is the third documentary in Marylou & Jerome Bongiorno’s 3Rs Trilogy on Urban America, following the success of critically acclaimed, award-winning, national PBS broadcast REVOLUTION ’67 (2007) on riots/rebellions of the 1960s and THE RULE (2014) on urban school reform. RUST presents the history of Rust Belt poverty, detailing industrialization and deindustrialization, racism and mass incarceration, using the city of Newark, New Jersey as a microcosm. It explores solutions to inner city poverty through the voices of scholars, economists, physicians, activists, and the community.  The filmmakers will lead then a lively discussion addressing questions about the filmmaking process and their process in documenting social justice issues.

No registration is required. Light refreshment will be served. Screening will be held on the 2nd Floor of the Library and will begin at 2:00 p.m.

To learn more about Bongiorno Productions visit: bongiornoproductions.com.

To view the trailer visit: https://vimeo.com/502830434.

Edwin Ortiz founded the “Returning Citizens Support Group” in Newark, which "provides critical reentry support services for systems-impacted communities of color.” To learn more visit: returningcitizensnj.org.

This program is made possible in part by funds from the New Jersey State Council on the Arts /  Department of State, a Partner Agency of the National Endowment for the Arts and administered by the Essex County Division of Cultural and Historic Affairs.

title: Annual March on Musikfest Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
join us for our annual March on Musikfest hike, and event we have been having for 26 years!
One would think that after so much time, we would have exhausted every way we could walk into this event, but this time we've found some more interesting stuff we've never done before!
This year, we will approach from the Southeast. our route will take us first along a pleasant preserve full of field Trails, and then along some pleasant back roads that are narrower than some of the trails we use. We will then get on another Greenway and make our way into hellertown. we will take a familiar trip North on the saucon rail trail, check out the Thomas Ironworks site again, and then other Trails as we continue to the north into Saucon Park.
Will continue to a new connecting trail in this area, and then mic our way back to the north Bethlehem. We will meander through the fest and then make our way North to where we met.
if needed, contact me at 908-343-8374

title: Long Pose Figure Drawing and Painting Session
description:
Tuesday Night Sessions:  Sunday Edition 
Sunday, August 2, 1 – 5 pm, $10 per hour or $35 for the full session 
“The object isn’t to make art, it’s to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri 
This special Sunday session is an extended version of our beloved Tuesday night figure drawing, giving you a full four hours to sink deep into the work. Bring your favorite materials, settle in, listen to some good tunes in great company, and get into your flow.  This will be a great opportunity to create a more finished work of art, hone your portraiture skills, or work with a material that you don’t normally get to use. 
Our model will be dressed in character (more details coming soon) and serve as our muse for the afternoon.  Whether you want to loosen up your line work, push into a sustained study, or simply spend a slow Sunday afternoon drawing from life, this is your space to do it. 
You can stay for the full session, or drop in and pay by the hour for an hour or two. 
All skill levels welcome, from seasoned studio artists to total beginners. Even poets have been known to drop in. 
Sunday, August 2 | 1:00 – 5:00 pm The Space, Montclair 
Materials such as charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paints are all welcome. Basic drawing supplies available upon request. No formal instruction is given so it is a self-guided session. 
Check out our regular weekly Tuesday night sessions here.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - The Legacy of Julia Child's Kitchen with Smithsonian Curator Paula J. Johnson
description:
You must register here to attend: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/160183

Join us for a conversation that’s sure to warm your heart (and make your stomach rumble), as we delve into the legacy of cooking icon Julia Child with Smithsonian curator and public historian Paula J. Johnson, author of Julia Child’s Kitchen: The Design, Tools, Stories, and Legacy of an Iconic Space. The book includes interviews with chefs who knew Julia well, commentary on her favorite culinary tools and kitchen gadgets, and a stunning array of photos.

Julia Child's 20’ x 14’ kitchen was a serious workspace and recipe‑testing lab that exuded a sense of mid‑century homey comfort. It has been on display at the National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C., for most of the past twenty-three years, and museum goers have made it a top destination.

The kitchen contains more than one thousand parts and pieces—tools, appliances, utensils, furniture, artwork, knick‑knacks, books, and bits of whimsy—all reflecting Julia’s status as an accomplished chef, gastronome, delightful cooking teacher, television trailblazer, women’s advocate, mentor, and generous, jovial friend.

Julia Child’s Kitchen (and this online conversation) is a must‑have for every serious home cook and Julia Child fan. Register now to enter the discussion and learn more about how Julia Child continues to influence food today!

About the Author: 

Paula J. Johnson is a curator and public historian at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History in Washington, DC. She conducts research and collects objects relating to the history and culture of American food and serves as the Director of the Smithsonian’s Food History Project. Johnson was one of the curators who collected Julia Child’s home kitchen in 2001 and led the team that created FOOD: Transforming the American Table, a multi-layered exhibition that explores the major changes in food production, distribution, and consumption in the United States since the 1950s. She has shaped and contributed to many public programs on food history and leads the annual “Food History Weekend.” Johnson is the author of many articles and three books, including Julia Child’s Kitchen: The Design, Tools Stories, and Legacy of an Iconic Space (2024). She received the Smithsonian Distinguished Scholar in the Humanities Award in 2020.

Johnson began her museum career at the Calvert Marine Museum in Solomons, Maryland, and has worked at the Smithsonian since 1991. She is a member of the Association for the Study of Food and Society and Les Dames d’ Escoffier. She serves on the editorial collective for Gastronomica: The Journal for Food Studies.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Native Vector Search in SQL Server 2025: Building AI-Ready Applications
description:
Cloud Data Driven
SQL Server 2025 extends the data platform with native vector search, enabling AI-powered similarity queries directly inside the database. New vector data types and built-in index structures allow efficient storage and querying of high-dimensional embeddings (e.g., from NLP or image models). With optimized Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms and vector indexes, queries achieve millisecond-level response times - even across millions of vectors.

We will explore how vector indexes optimize performance by accelerating similarity searches and reducing resource consumption, while also discussing their limitations - such as index build times, storage overhead, and scenarios where approximate results may differ from exact matches.
Beyond the database engine, you will see how SQL Server 2025 integrates with Azure Foundry and Azure OpenAI Service, enabling embeddings generated by text and image models to be ingested directly into SQL via API calls. This allows developers to build end-to-end pipelines where model outputs are stored, indexed, and queried in real time - without external search infrastructure.

Use cases include real-time personalized recommendations, semantic analytics, and anomaly detection for security scenarios, all running on your proven SQL platform. Seamless integration with Azure hybrid scenarios enables vector search to scale across on-premises and cloud environments, while enterprise-grade features such as role-based access control and Always Encrypted ensure secure handling of sensitive embeddings.

By the end of this session, you will understand how to leverage SQL Server 2025’s native vector search, vector indexes, and AI integration to build scalable, secure, and intelligent applications - while being aware of their trade-offs and best practices for real-world deployments.

description:

In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We meet at 9AM unless one or more people comment wanting to meet at 8AM which is my preferred time. You’re welcome to show up any time but are encouraged to post it so we have a better idea of what to expect for that day. (Those who share the same comment for start time can simply like that comment so we see how many show up for that time without potentially cluttering the comments.)

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll follow my Florida instructor’s method for balanced clinic matches\. This will typically include quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages team clotting\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis And More
We meet at 9AM unless one or more people comment wanting to meet at 8AM which is my preferred time. You’re welcome to show up any time but are encouraged to post it so we have a better idea of what to expect for that day. (Those who share the same comment for start time can simply like that comment so we see how many show up for that time without potentially cluttering the comments.)

**RULES:** By signing up you agree to follow these rules:

1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. If two or more people are in agreement then they’re welcome to exchange instructions so long as they relinquish their court positions and don’t disrupt active players\. If anyone is instructing or ordering you and you’re not comfortable then please tell them or let me know\. Everyone should feel free to play however they wish without being directed without agreement\, most especially beginners\.

2\. No formal matches are allowed on any of our group\-reserved courts\. If people are in agreement then they’re welcome to find another court not in use by our group to play strict matches\. If we need to rotate people in and out due to lack of enough courts then we’ll follow my Florida instructor’s method for balanced clinic matches\. This will typically include quick matches to 5 points after which everyone rotates clockwise one position\. This keeps those waiting rotated back in often and also discourages team clotting\.

3\. We are foremost beginner\-friendly and not aggressively competitive or an instruction\-oriented group\. A little light and friendly competition or giving a quick tip so long as you’re not holding up the court is OK but please pace yourself against the person you’re hitting to \(e\.g\. hit softer to members that might not be as good or as aggressive as you\)\. Everyone should be made to feel welcome and free regardless of skill level\. Beginners most especially should always feel comfortable here\.

4\. Please make sure you’re signed up using a name that matches your Meetup name\. New players should always check in with me so I can mark you down as having checked in\. Anyone showing up without a Meetup RSVP will be asked to do so before they can participate in the event\. If you’re bringing one guest that’s fine\, just make sure to mark them on your RSVP\.

5\. If I feel you’re consistently not following the rules I have the right to ask you to relinquish your position on the court\. Please don’t sign up and attend if you don’t agree to following any one rule here\. We are largely democratic but I reserve the right to make any final calls if I deem it necessary for any reason\, such as breaking up and remixing long\-locked groups if we have more than one court\.

**EQUIPMENT:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: (FULL) Everything Book Club, "The Sum of Us" by Heather McGhee
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
Join this session as part of our community read and receive a free copy of "The Sum of Us: What Racism Costs All of Us and How We Can Prosper Together" while supplies last, thanks to Partners for Health Foundation! For more details and related events, go to Montclair Reads "The Sum of Us." The community read will culminate with a live Open Book / Open Mind author conversation with Heather McGhee on Tuesday, October 13 at 7 p.m. 

If you’re sick of the antagonism and zero-sum-game thinking so prevalent in American public life today, you’ll find a refreshing antidote in this still timely landmark bestseller from 2021. What if we've been thinking about opportunity in America all wrong? What if instead of groups trying to get a larger slice of the pie, we all worked together to create a bigger, better pie? Economist Heather McGhee goes on a road trip across the country asking "why can't we have nice things?" and is surprised to encounter in a variety of towns, workplaces and houses of worship what she calls "the Solidarity Dividend"—what we gain when people come together across race and other differences to accomplish what we simply can’t do on our own. Could we find it in our own hometown? 

“Every so often a book comes along that seems perfectly timed to the moment and has the potential to radically shift our cultural conversation. [The Sum of Us] is one of those books.—Chicago Tribune 

Heather McGhee is an expert in economic and social policy. The former president of the inequality-focused think tank Demos, McGhee now chairs the board of Color of Change, the nation’s largest online racial justice organization.

description:

Julia Strayer and Liz Maccarone will lead a lively and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio.

This is a virtual program that takes place over Zoom. As the date approaches, you will receive an email with the Zoom link.

About the Presenters

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Previously, Julia worked in marketing for 9 years with Merrill. Julia has a BA from Ohio State University and an MBA from New York University’s Stern School of Business. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. Liz works closely with high-net-worth individuals and their families to create personalized and comprehensive strategies that support their goals, including investment management, retirement planning, liability management, and multigenerational planning. Liz values the importance of establishing and cultivating relationships with families including the next generation. Liz graduated from Fairfield University with a dual bachelor’s degree in Finance and Marketing. She began her career working at a boutique investment firm as a Business Development Associate, specializing in commodities and futures trading.

title: (FULL) Everything Book Club, "The Sum of Us" by Heather McGhee
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
Join this session as part of our community read and receive a free copy of "The Sum of Us: What Racism Costs All of Us and How We Can Prosper Together" while supplies last, thanks to Partners for Health Foundation! For more details and related events, go to Montclair Reads "The Sum of Us." The community read will culminate with a live Open Book / Open Mind author conversation with Heather McGhee on Tuesday, October 13 at 7 p.m. 

If you’re sick of the antagonism and zero-sum-game thinking so prevalent in American public life today, you’ll find a refreshing antidote in this still timely landmark bestseller from 2021. What if we've been thinking about opportunity in America all wrong? What if instead of groups trying to get a larger slice of the pie, we all worked together to create a bigger, better pie? Economist Heather McGhee goes on a road trip across the country asking "why can't we have nice things?" and is surprised to encounter in a variety of towns, workplaces and houses of worship what she calls "the Solidarity Dividend"—what we gain when people come together across race and other differences to accomplish what we simply can’t do on our own. Could we find it in our own hometown? 

“Every so often a book comes along that seems perfectly timed to the moment and has the potential to radically shift our cultural conversation. [The Sum of Us] is one of those books.—Chicago Tribune 

Heather McGhee is an expert in economic and social policy. The former president of the inequality-focused think tank Demos, McGhee now chairs the board of Color of Change, the nation’s largest online racial justice organization.

title: 3rd Annual Student Art Exhibition & Film Screening
UNRECYCLABLE:  Look Again - Assemblage Art by Andrew Borg
description:
UNRECYCLABLE: Look Again – Assemblage Art by Andrew Borg 
Opening Reception:  Friday, August 14, 5 – 8pm 
The Space presents Unrecyclable: Look Again, a solo exhibition of assemblage art by Andrew Borg composed predominantly of the unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites he refused to throw away for nearly two years — the molded trays, caps, and packaging inserts that carry no recycling code and vanish into the trash without a thought. The exhibition, culminating Borg’s year as Artist in Residence at The Space, is on view August 14–22, 2026, with an opening reception Friday, August 14, from 5 to 8pm. 
What began as an act of defiance gradually became an act of appreciation: these are highly engineered, purpose-built objects, molded to cushion, position, and protect — aesthetic objects in their own right, designed by someone, meant to be forgotten by everyone. 
The assemblage artworks in Unrecyclable: Look Again are composed from that two-year collection. The work asks viewers to make a conscious choice to look again — at the craft embedded in what we discard, and at our own constant contributions to a stream of toxic materials that will outlast us by generations. 
“I collected these objects for almost two years before I fully understood why. Refusing to throw them away began as an act of defiance. Over time, it became an obsession, to look at them as raw material for re-expression — aesthetic objects with a conscience,” says Borg. 
In keeping with Montclair’s participatory community spirit, the public is invited to create their own assemblage artworks during the opening reception, using unrecyclable materials and art supplies provided by the gallery. 
The exhibition closes with a Gallery Talk & Assemblage Lab on Saturday, August 22, 1–3pm. Borg gives a gallery talk, then leads a hands-on session in which participants re-see “ghost objects” — abandoned electronics and appliances — and combine them with other unrecyclable materials to build assemblages of their own. All materials provided; no prior artistic experience required.  Register here. 
Borg was invited to mount the exhibition by The Space founder Naz Botas, following his year in residence. 
About the Artist: Andrew Borg is an assemblage artist and 2025–26 Artist in Residence at The Space in Montclair, NJ. Trained in painting at Harvard, he danced professionally in NYC for nine years, then spent four decades in technology innovation. His current series asks us to look again at what we throw away.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - August meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

\*your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,

* What you can help others with,
\*What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

title: Introduction to Wheel Throwing Pottery NEW
description:
Note: This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Discover the art of working on the potter’s wheel in this hands-on 6-week introductory course. Whether you're a complete beginner or looking to refine basic skills, this class offers a welcoming environment to explore the fundamentals of working with clay on the wheel.

You’ll learn the essential techniques of centering, pulling, shaping, and trimming clay to create functional forms like bowls and cups. As the course progresses, you’ll be introduced to glazing methods and the firing process, transforming your pieces into finished, food-safe ceramics. By the end of the session, you’ll have several unique, handmade pieces to take home and enjoy.

All clay, glaze, firings and tools are included.

For the first class, bring an apron or work clothes, sketchbook, writing implement and your curiosity!

title: Write to the Mic Dodge Poetry Teen Workshops
description: Everyone’s voice is different. We want to hear  yours . This winter/spring, come together with other teens (ages 13 to 18) from across Newark at a  Dodge Poetry workshop  designed to showcase your words and ideas. Poets from the community ( like   Newark’s first-ever poet laureate, Mia X ), and students from the  Rutgers-Newark MFA program in Poetry , will be on hand to offer prompts, suggestions and ideas. But the focus is on you:  What frustrates you? Where do you find joy? What does this city and this country look like from your unique, powerful perspective? We believe poetry can be found in books, but also in hip hop, at protests and parties, in the clip of a song playing from the window of a passing car.  Poetry is an oral tradition , especially here in Newark. (Even our  mayor  is a spoken word artist; this is what we do!) So be a part of the conversation. Join us to write your own verses, and then (if you choose) speak them out loud at the  open mic that ends every session . Workshops are FREE  and will be held in person on the first Wednesday of the month (at locations in various wards in Newark; see below for details) and virtually on the third Wednesday of the month. THEME: Youth Poetry Workshop (Ages 13-18) / Open Mic HOST: NJPAC FEATURES: Poets from the community ( like   Newark’s first-ever poet laureate, Mia X ), and students from the  Rutgers-Newark MFA program in Poetry , will be on hand to offer prompts, suggestions and ideas. title: Tea & Tarot - A Bookclub Style Discussion Group with Gina Devine
description:
Tea & Tarot: A book club style discussion group with Gina Devine
Monthly Gathering | Friday, August 21th | 7:00 PM – 8:30 PM | The Space | $25 
Calling all tarot lovers, both new and seasoned!  Join us for an intimate way of exploring the cards. 
What could be better than a cozy evening of warm tea and deep conversation? Join us for Tea & Tarot with Gina Devine—a monthly, book club-style discussion group created to deepen our connection with the archetypes of the tarot through community and shared insight. 
Rather than a formal class, this is a casual meet-up where we treat the tarot as a living text. Based on the psychological insights of Carl Jung, we will explore the Major Arcana not just as fortune-telling tools, but as mirrors of our own lives, rituals, and transformations. 
The Experience 
Each month, we open a new gateway of creative and spiritual exploration. Our time together includes: 

Archetypal Deep Dives: We’ll focus on a specific theme or set of cards each session, discussing their symbolism and how they show up in our modern world.
Collaborative Readings: A chance to pull cards for one another in a supportive, low-pressure environment.
Ritual & Connection: We’ll sip tea, share stories, and find common ground in the mysteries of the deck.
Intuitive Growth: Whether you’ve been reading for decades or just bought your first deck, you’ll leave with a deeper understanding of the “BodyGraph” of the tarot.

What to Bring 
To make the most of our evening, please bring the following if you can: 

Your Tarot Deck: Any deck you feel connected to.  If you don’t have any we have some available here to use.
Your Favorite Mug: We’ll provide a selection of teas, and don’t worry if you don’t bring your mug – we have those too!
A Notebook: For capturing insights, spreads, and “aha” moments.

Investment: $25 
Stay Connected: Sign up for the Soul Centric Tarot Newsletter here. 
Spaces are limited to keep our discussion intimate and impactful. Reserve your spot today and join the circle. 
Cover art by Sophie Bryant Funnell 
______________________________ 

Your Guide Gina Devine
Instagram: @gina.devine 

Gina Devine is an esoteric artist, intuitive tarot reader, writer, educator and guide. 
She has provided thousands of readings for people all over the world, and leads both protection and tarot workshops. Her approach to guidance is loving, grounded and human. Although she also teaches traditional tarot classes, her tea and tarot discussion group was birthed from the knowing that people are more inclined to to be in tune with the archetypes of the cards and the messages they bring when they are allowed space to enjoy the tarot in a more casual setting – instead of forcefully trying to memorize them. The same way we find joy in discussing a book in community, the cards also call for us to convene together around them. Her approach is philosophical, therapeutic and creative, and she is on a mission to guide people toward unearthing a more intimate and honest relationship with their inner knowing through the art of divination. You can find her services and more at soulcentrictarot.com

title: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg
description:
Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg
Closing Event for “Unrecyclable: Look Again” 
What do you see when you really look at what you throw away? 
Join artist Andrew Borg for the closing event of Unrecyclable: Look Again — an afternoon that begins with a gallery talk and ends with your hands deep in materials you never thought twice about discarding. 
After walking through the exhibition and sharing the story behind his two-year collection of unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites, Borg leads an immersive hands-on Assemblage Lab in which participants get to experience the process firsthand. Using unrecyclable packaging, abandoned electronics, appliances, and other “ghost objects,” you’ll build your own assemblage, sculpture, or mixed-media artwork — guided by the same impulse that drove this exhibition: look again. 
No artistic experience required. No right or wrong. Just a fresh set of eyes and a willingness to see the overlooked as raw material for something new. 
Unrecyclable materials are provided, along with glue to put your assemblages together. Bring your own materials too — packaging, foam inserts, bottle caps, old electronics, anything you’ve been meaning to throw away. The stranger the better. 
🗓 Saturday, August 22 | 1:00 pm – 3:00 pm
📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, 2nd Floor, Montclair, NJ
🎟 $10 
Part gallery talk, part art lab, all creative. Come ready to make something!

title: Unearthing Our Past: Revolutionary Stories
description:
Unearthing Our Past: Revolutionary Stories

Presented by West Orange Township Historian Joseph Fagan

West Orange Public Library – August 22, 2026 – 2pm

 

Join West Orange Township Historian Joseph Fagan as he unearths the many stories forgotten by time at the Old Burying Ground in nearby Orange. Here weathered gravestones and forgotten burial plots reveal the many stories of West Orange’s first settlers. Join Joseph Fagan as he steps through an undisturbed portal in time where Revolutionary War patriots, local families, and ordinary citizens still bear silent witness to history. Discover the stories of the people whose lives, sacrifices, and experiences helped shape both our local community and the nation.

 

Presented as part of the commemoration of America’s 250th anniversary, this program is the second in a series by Joseph Fagan supporting Rev250 NJ. It is a statewide initiative that explores the unique Revolutionary War history of communities across New Jersey. Join Fagan for an engaging journey into the people, events, and stories that helped define our nation and continue to shape our local heritage today.

description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this interesting loop hike in the Shawangunks of New York!
For this 15 mile loop trip, we will meet at the Foordmore Trailhead for the Long Path near Kerkhonksen New York.
The most difficult parts will be the very beginning where we ascend the Shawangunk Ridge on backroads and the Stony Kill Carriageway.
Once we reach the top of the ridge, we continue a bit through the blueberry lands, and then descend a bit on Smiley Carriageway. There will be one rough bit of trail down to a waterfall, and then more pleasant back roads. There is one bit that has metal rungs to climb up, but it is quite short. I'll be prepared with a pack to carry all of Ev's stuff for this stretch.
The only regular road walk stuff is pretty much at the very beginning, and the beginning of the ascent.
Once we do the entire ridge bit, two thirds of the hike, we'll make our way onto the Delaware and Hudson Canal, as well as the O&W Rail Trail.
This will provide us with an easy creekside walk for the last stretch.
Apart from two difficult miles, the rest of the hike should be very relaxing.
The gradual climb will be on back road and dirt road, and then trail. After that, we have ten miles of gradual downhill to flat.
There are going to be a few stores in Ellenville at mile 11 or 12, but otherwise there are no other stores along the way.

title: Reimagining the Tarot: An Intuitive Collage Workshop
description:
Reimagining the Tarot: An Intuitive Collage Workshop
What if the Tarot could speak in your voice? 
In this exploratory workshop, we’ll dive into the rich history and symbolism of the Major Arcana — exploring the colors, archetypes, and allegories that have given these iconic cards their power for centuries. Then, we’ll turn that wisdom over to your own creative instincts. 
No art experience needed. No tarot experience needed. Just an open mind and a willingness to listen to what’s stirring inside you. 
You’ll choose a card that calls to you, journal your reflections, and then bring it to life through drawing, painting, or collage — reimagining it through your own symbols, style, and personal expression. The goal isn’t perfection; it’s presence. We’re letting intuition lead. 
📅 Sunday, August 23 | 12:00 pm – 3:00 pm 📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Loft #2, Montclair, NJ 🎟 $50 | Returning participants: $30 (arrive at 1:30 pm) 
What You’ll Do: 

Explore the Major Arcana and the art of symbolic storytelling
Choose a card that resonates with you in the moment
Journal your insights and reflections
Sketch and plan your own symbolic design
Create your unique version of the card through your medium of choice.  Collage materials, magazines, paint, colored pencils and markers will be available.

All materials provided. Just bring your imagination, an open mind, a tarot deck, and a notebook. 
This is an ongoing series — each session builds on the last. Returning participants are welcome to skip the first segment and join at 1:30 pm for the creative portion only with a $30 ticket. 
  
Your Guide Gina Devine
Instagram: @gina.devine 

Gina Devine is an esoteric artist, intuitive tarot reader, writer, educator and guide. 
She has provided thousands of readings for people all over the world, and leads both protection and tarot workshops. Her approach to guidance is loving, grounded and human. Although she also teaches traditional tarot classes, her tea and tarot discussion group was birthed from the knowing that people are more inclined to to be in tune with the archetypes of the cards and the messages they bring when they are allowed space to enjoy the tarot in a more casual setting – instead of forcefully trying to memorize them. The same way we find joy in discussing a book in community, the cards also call for us to convene together around them. Her approach is philosophical, therapeutic and creative, and she is on a mission to guide people toward unearthing a more intimate and honest relationship with their inner knowing through the art of divination. You can find her services and more at soulcentrictarot.com

title: Mental Health Support Group (NAMI's Connection Recovery Peer Support Group)
description:
The Essex-Passaic Chapter of NAMI (The National Alliance on Mental Illness) Connection Recovery Peer Support Group Program meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month at the West Caldwell Library on 30 Clinton Road. 

NAMI is the most influential organization devoted to helping people with mental illness and their relatives and loved ones recover and deal with mental health issues. These meetings will be led by people having some form of mental illness. During these meetings, we will conduct peer support though all people interested in this organization are encouraged to attend. You do not have to sign up in advance. All meetings are kept confidential and are led by people specifically trained to conduct these meetings.

 NAMI Connection is a recovery peer support group program that offers respect, understanding, encouragement and hope. NAMI Connection groups are:

·       Free and confidential

·       Held monthly for 90 minutes  

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - High Altitudes and High Stakes: A Miss Marple Mystery with Lucy Foley
description:
You must register here to attend: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/187080

Join us for a thrilling conversation with acclaimed author Lucy Foley as we delve into her brand-new Miss Marple mystery, Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel. 

High in the Swiss Alps, accessible only by a single, winding railway, stands the luxurious Grand Alpine Hotel. With glorious mountain views and exclusive access to powdery slopes, it draws guests from far and wide. 

The notorious actress. 

The high-flying politician. 

The society wife. 

The reckless friend. 

The shrewd doctor. 

But not everyone is here for a winter holiday. Beneath the champagne and furs, dark histories simmer; old grudges emerge like cracks in the ice. And someone is watching from the shadows. A polite, unassuming woman with an extraordinary mind: Miss Marple. When a body is found and a blizzard cuts off all escape, only Miss Marple can connect the clues before the killer strikes again. Because it isn’t a question of who has a motive, but who’s next…

About the Author:

Lucy Foley is a No.1 Sunday Times, Irish Times and New York Times bestselling author. More than 10 million copies of her books are in print worldwide, and several are currently being adapted for the screen. She is a Waterstones Thriller of the Month author, a three-time nominee at the British Book Awards, and The Guest List was a Reese’s Book Club selection and winner of the Goodreads Choice Award for Mystery Thriller. As a life-long Agatha Christie fan, Lucy has drawn immeasurable inspiration from the Queen of Crime. She was one of 12 writers to contribute to Marple, a collection of short stories featuring the beloved detective. And in Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel, she was inspired to transport Miss Marple – her favorite Christie creation – to the glamorous post-war setting of the Swiss Alps, in a mystery that feels gloriously escapist yet utterly relevant to our times.

description:
This month we will be reading "Fruit Fly" by Josh Silver.

A BBC must-read book of 2026—”Sharp, dark and humorous, it’s a real nail-biter.”

Go gay. Go sad. Go dark.

A washed-up author will stop at nothing to claw her way back to relevancy—even if it means appropriating a young gay man’s tragic story.

Mallory Maddox is buried under seven years of writer’s block. With her status as a literary sensation fizzling, she’ll do anything she can to resurrect her career. Inspiration needs to strike—and fast.

Enter Leo. He’s a struggling addict sleeping under bridges and trading sex for survival. He’s vulnerable. He’s enigmatic. He’s exactly what Mallory has been looking for. 

Mallory needs Leo if she wants another bestseller. The world needs Leo’s story right now, and Mallory believes she deserves to tell it. Really, it’s her story—she’s the one who wrote it, after all. 

But as secrets threaten to unravel more than just her career, Mallory must decide how far she will go to pen the perfect story. 

A razor-sharp satirical thriller, Fruit Fly will appeal to fans of R. F. Kuang’s Yellowface and Yomi Adegoke’s The List.

This event is for anyone who has previously attended Tarot 101 with Kate and/or gained basic tarot skills independently. If you’re familiar with the Major and Minor Arcana and you know how to shuffle and pull the cards, then you’re ready for 201!

During our time together, Kate will explore in more depth the esoteric and spiritual principles behind the tarot, particularly the Major Arcana as seen through the lens of Jungian psychology. Taking us along the Fool’s Journey, Kate will offer card interpretations that continue to move beyond making predictions and instead focus on conscious evolution and soul growth.

Attendees are encouraged to bring a notebook and pen, plus your favorite tarot deck (if you have one). The program will begin with an extended Q&A troubleshooting session, particularly for those who have attended Tarot 101, so feel free to come prepared with questions!

While this program is designed with relative beginners in mind, more intermediate tarot learners may benefit from this in-depth review of foundational concepts.

About the presenter: Kate Sheridan, a.k.a. The Laundress, is a tarot reader and astrologer who believes that each one of us can make our own magic. Her approach is healing rather than predictive, and her work is deeply informed by Jungian psychology. You can find her on Instagram @themodernlaundress or online at thelaundresstarot.com.

description:
Information

A method that takes an investigative approach to the study of family history and genealogy. In this presentation, you will hear from a historian who has 25 years of experience doing investigations on innovative approaches to genealogy and how to think differently. There is a wide range of topics that can be covered in this course, ranging from the foundations of using Ancestry and establishing a family tree to more advanced topics such as overcoming brick walls and delving deeper into historical and genealogical material.

Summer World Literature Series

THE ART OF LOSING 
by Alice Zeniter (France)
translated by Frank Wynne

Naïma's family comes from Algeria, but she knows it only from what she experiences in her grandparents' tiny apartment in Normandy: the food her grandmother cooks, the precious things they carried when they fled. Naïma's father claims to remember nothing, has made himself French. But now, one of them is going back and Naïma will see for herself what was left behind, including the family secrets. A powerful, moving family novel that spans three generations, across seventy years and two shores of the Mediterranean Sea.

title: Hike with Dr. Kirk! 3-4 miles
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**Saturday, August 29 4-7pm**

Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation.

Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the Rahway River up South Mountain. title: Brandywine Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point 15 mile hike, the next in the Brandywine Series!
This time, we'll travel between Delacy Soccer Complex in East Bradford Township and Downingtown.
We already covered some of Downingtown previously, but this time we'll cover some other municipal trails and former route of the Brandywine Trail near the beginning, as well as the end of Struble Trail, Lions Trail, and we'll trace the historic route of the Pennsylvania Railroad New Holland Branch briefly.
From here, we take some new creekside trails, and then make our way on the Brandywine Trail up to the Philadelphia and Thorndale Branch. We take another municipal trail from here south to a pleasant back road with no lines in it, and then revisit the Harmony Hill Covered Bridge.
Along this stretch, we'll follow the alternate Brandywine Trail we saw previously, out to Sugar's Bridge.
From here, the Brandywine Trail follows a pleasant back road bit down to the Natural Land Trust Stroud Preserve.
We will hike the Stroud Preserve trails that we'd not explored before, then make our way south along Brandywine Trail to Jeffers Ford.
Another brief road walk leads us to another foot path section, then a short back road to an abandoned road which will lead us down to our end point.
The only place we pass any store on this one is in Downingtown near the beginning, so everyone should come prepared with all they need!
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Long Pose Figure Drawing and Painting Session
description:
Tuesday Night Sessions:  Sunday Edition 
Sunday, August 30, 1 – 5 pm, $10 per hour or $35 for the full session 
“The object isn’t to make art, it’s to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri 
This special Sunday session is an extended version of our beloved Tuesday night figure drawing, giving you a full four hours to sink deep into the work. Bring your favorite materials, settle in, listen to some good tunes in great company, and get into your flow.  This will be a great opportunity to create a more finished work of art, hone your portraiture skills, or work with a material that you don’t normally get to use. 
Our model will be dressed in character (more details coming soon) and serve as our muse for the afternoon.  Whether you want to loosen up your line work, push into a sustained study, or simply spend a slow Sunday afternoon drawing from life, this is your space to do it. 
You can stay for the full session, or drop in and pay by the hour for an hour or two. 
All skill levels welcome, from seasoned studio artists to total beginners. Even poets have been known to drop in. 
Sunday, August 30 | 1:00 – 5:00 pm The Space, Montclair 
Materials such as charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paints are all welcome. Basic drawing supplies available upon request. No formal instruction is given so it is a self-guided session.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - The Democracy We Must Keep: Why the Ideas that Built America Still Matter with David O. Stewart
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/195262

Join us as we chat with award-winning historian David O. Stewart about his newest work, The Democracy We Must Keep, and the question he explores throughout the book: What did America's founders say about democracy, and can we remain true to their vision for America?

Two hundred fifty years ago, passionate men attempted to create something the world had never seen before: a nation built not on kings or armies, but on ideas where the people ruled.

In The Democracy We Must Keep, historian David O. Stewart takes readers inside the nine key documents that shaped the formation of the United States—from Patrick Henry's thunderous cry for liberty to the carefully crafted design of a government chosen by the people, with limits on all officials holding power under the Constitution.

Through the words of seven visionary founders—Washington, Jefferson, Madison, Hamilton, Gouverneur Morris, and others—Stewart shows how a fragile experiment in self-government took shape.

These men were not saints. They argued passionately. They worried that the new nation might fall apart. Yet together, they forged the principles that must still define American democracy:


	Power must be limited.
	Leaders must answer to the people.
	Individual rights must be protected by law.


As the United States celebrates its 250th anniversary, The Democracy We Must Keep urges readers to rediscover core ideas that built the nation—and to consider what it will take to protect them.

Register today to gain a deeper understanding of how American democracy started, why it still matters, and the active role each generation must play to uphold it.

About the Author: 

David O. Stewart has published eleven award-winning and best-selling books of history and historical novels. In 2023, he received the Lifetime Achievement Award of the Washington Independent Review of Books. His most recent fictional series, the Overstreet Saga, is inspired by family stories his mother told. He lives in Maryland with the light of his life, Nancy Floreen; they have three children and six grandchildren

description:

As Shabbat comes to a close, children and adults will come together to recite Havdalah prayers. We are looking forward to having our children who are 8 yrs old and up help lead the havdalah candle lighting ceremony while reciting prayers with Rabbi Julie.

**------------------------------**

**Have questions? Want to Help out? Contact:** Shomrei Office  
office@shomrei.org  
(973) 746-5031

**What is Selichot?**  
The Hebrew word selichah means “forgiveness.” The plural form of the word selichah is selichot, a word traditionally used to refer to additional prayers for forgiveness recited during the month of Elul (through Yom Kippur). We gather together on the Saturday night before Rosh Hashanah to meditate on the capacity for forgiveness and on its power. In joining together we help each other pray for that blessing – to give it and to receive it.

title: Is Your Marketing Built for Your Current Stage of Growth?
description:
Montclair Business Networking
What worked when your business was smaller may be slowing your growth now.
Growth requires change, but many companies don’t evolve their marketing strategy quickly enough.
The systems, team structure, processes, and investments that made sense at one stage can create inefficiency, inconsistent lead flow, or missed opportunities at the next stage.
So, how do you know if your marketing is where it should be?
On September 8 at 12 PM ET, join us for a virtual discussion on how marketing, sales, and operational strategies should evolve as businesses grow, and what companies at each stage should be doing differently.
What You’ll Learn

* Which marketing systems, automation tools, and infrastructure make sense at different stages of growth
* When to hire internally, outsource strategically, or keep marketing lean based on your company’s size, complexity, and growth goals
* What processes growing companies typically need to formalize to create more consistency and scalability
* How to strengthen lead generation, follow-up, sales alignment, and execution as your business becomes more complex
* The common mistakes companies make when their marketing doesn’t evolve with their growth

Who Should Attend

* Business owners and executives questioning whether their current marketing approach can support the next stage of growth
* Sales, marketing, and operations leaders responsible for driving revenue and efficiency
* Companies building, restructuring, or scaling
* Organizations looking to create more predictable growth without unnecessary overhead

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Writing the Nightmare: A Ship Called Sickness and One Unforgettable Space Crew with Daniel Kraus
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/194581

Prepare to launch into the darkest depths of deep space! Join us as we sit down with master storyteller Daniel Kraus, winner of the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, to celebrate the release of his breathtaking new novel, The Sixth Nik.

Deep into space, far past the triworld outposts, beyond range of the lethal trollbot internet, soars The Sickness: a ship woven from biomatter and capable of reacting to every need of its human crew. Sisilla, a nine-year-old cultist with a brain enhanced by arcane tech known as “niks,” has boarded to investigate the enigma of Fém—a plague-riddled planet that has abruptly gone rogue.

The mysterious crew includes a faceless assassin, a beautiful engineer jigsawed by plastic surgery, a peyote-addicted medic, and—most lethal of all—a rugged, NonModded captain with a score to settle with Sisilla. Other dangers abound. A hacked robot begins to believe Sisilla is its daughter. The Sickness itself is mutating, possibly even pregnant. And the secret of Fém is more horrific than anyone could have imagined. To survive, Sisilla will need to forsake her predetermined fate and embrace the unknown.

Register now to gain exclusive insight from one of the most visionary voices in modern fiction.

About the Author:

Daniel Kraus is a Pulitzer Prize-winning, New York Times bestselling writer of novels, TV, and film. His novel Angel Down was the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction winner, a New York Times Top 10 Book of 2025, and a national bestseller. His novel Whalefall received a front-cover review in the New York Times Book Review, won the Alex Award, was an L.A. Times Book Prize Finalist, and was a Best Book of 2023 from NPR, the New York Times, Amazon, Chicago Tribune, and more.

With Guillermo del Toro, he co-authored The Shape of Water, based on the same idea the two created for the Oscar-winning film. Also with del Toro, Kraus co-authored Trollhunters, which was adapted into the Emmy-winning Netflix series. He co-wrote The Living Dead and Pay the Piper with legendary filmmaker George A. Romero. Kraus’s The Death and Life of Zebulon Finch was named one of Entertainment Weekly‘s Top 10 Books of the Year. Kraus has won the Bram Stoker Award, Scribe Award, two Odyssey Awards (for both Rotters and Scowler), and has appeared multiple times as Library Guild selections, and more.

Kraus’s work has been translated into over 25 languages. He lives with his partner in Chicago. Visit him at danielkraus.com

title: Creating a High School Roadmap - Parent & Teen Program
location: Glen Ridge - Meeting Room, Glen Ridge Free Public Library
description:
Families with students in grades 8 through 12 often arrive at junior year with very little sense of how the pieces fit together — coursework, extracurriculars, testing timelines, and applications. Until now.

In the workshop, attendees will walk away with:

       A clear picture of what each grade, 8 through 12,  should look like academically and outside the classroom

       An understanding of standardized testing timelines and how to approach them without last-minute stress

       A grounded overview of the college application and financial aid process, broken down by year

       Practical language for opening productive conversations between parents and students about goals, course selection, and next steps

Parent & Teen Program | Registration Required
OPEN to all

About the Presenter: Kevin Wallace is a licensed master social worker and co-founder of Full Circle College and Career Prep, based in Teaneck, NJ. Alongside his co-presenter, Cheryl Varghese, who holds a Master of Science in School Counseling, they work directly with high school students and families across northern New Jersey.

title: Zoom: Successfully Navigating College Admissions
description:
Register HERE





We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores, and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and how to successfully navigate today’s changing landscape.

 

The session will cover current college admissions trends and strategies, the evolving test optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find the right fit, and key timelines and action steps that can make this fall productive while easing stress around the college admissions process.

 

We will also take a close look at the holistic admissions review process, including what admissions officers value when evaluating applicants and how students can develop a strong personal narrative that reflects their strengths, interests, character, and experiences.

 

Another focus will be on the role of community service and the growing importance of meaningful “passion projects.” We will discuss how students can turn their interests, values, and experiences into authentic activities that foster personal growth, demonstrate character, and show positive impact. Admissions officers place great emphasis on character, and thoughtful service can help students show initiative, empathy, and a genuine commitment to helping their communities.

 

This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens. It provides a clear and strategic overview of what students should prioritize this fall for a successful college admissions journey and how to approach the process with confidence and less stress.

 

The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www.standoutforcollege.com).

title: A.I.M by Kyle Abraham: White Space
description:
Run Time: 1 hour 
White Space brings together acclaimed composers, Jason Moran and Nico Muhly, for a haunting new collaborative score that pierces the heart of choreographer Kyle Abraham’s newest evening-length dance. At just over one hour, this dance work grounds its cast of 11 captivating dancers in a restless and thought-provoking world fueled by a vast movement vocabulary consisting of Abraham’s signature blend of classical and contemporary dance with a hip-hop underbelly. The score is performed live by two pianists on one piano, with echoes of pre-recorded hip-hop driving the collision of reality and idealism. 
“lush movement, infectious music and magnetic dancers…” (The New York Times) 
 
About A.I.M by Kyle Abraham: Celebrating its 20th anniversary throughout 2016, A.I.M by Kyle Abraham has, for nearly two decades, been at the forefront of contemporary dance, becoming one of the most acclaimed touring companies in the world. A.I.M has been featured in Vogue, Essence, among many other publications, and was on the April 2025 cover of the Harper’s Bazaar. The company is described as a “postmodern gumbo” with an ardent voice and artistic process informed by robust conversations with people from diverse perspectives. A.I.M performs works by Abraham as well as new and existing works by choreographers who have influenced Abraham’s artistry.

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.
